disclaimer: Informational, not legal advice. Kavach does not file reports.

regimes.name: GDPR Art. 33 personal data breach
regimes.trigger: Personal data breach likely to result in a risk to individuals' rights and freedoms
regimes.applies_to: Controllers (processors must alert the controller without undue delay)

stages.name: Notify supervisory authority
stages.description: Without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware; reasons required if later

regimes.notes: Confirmed 2026-11-16: EDPB Guidelines 9/2022 (read directly) restate Art. 33(1): notify "not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it", with reasons for any delay. EUR-Lex pages returned empty to the research tool, so the statute itself was read only through the EDPB quotation. National transposition and supervisory-authority portals were not checked.

regimes.name: NIS2 Art. 23 significant incident
regimes.trigger: Significant incident affecting an essential or important entity
regimes.applies_to: Essential and important entities under NIS2 (as transposed nationally)

stages.name: Early warning
stages.description: Within 24 hours of becoming aware of a significant incident

stages.name: Incident notification
stages.description: Within 72 hours of becoming aware

stages.name: Final report
stages.description: No later than one month after the incident notification (progress report first if the incident is still ongoing)

regimes.notes: Confirmed 2026-11-16 from a search-result excerpt of the EUR-Lex text of Art. 23(4) (direct fetch of EUR-Lex returned empty): early warning within 24 hours of awareness, incident notification within 72 hours, intermediate report only on request, final report not later than one month after the incident notification (progress report if still ongoing). Trust service providers: 24 hours instead of 72. National transposition differences were not checked.

regimes.name: DORA major ICT-related incident
regimes.trigger: Incident classified as major under the DORA classification RTS
regimes.applies_to: Financial entities in scope of DORA

stages.name: Initial notification
stages.description: Within 4 hours of classifying as major and no later than 24 hours after awareness

stages.name: Intermediate report
stages.description: Within 72 hours of the initial notification

stages.name: Final report
stages.description: No later than one month after the latest intermediate report

regimes.notes: Confirmed 2026-11-16: Delegated Regulation 2025/301 Art. 5 per a search-result excerpt of the EUR-Lex text (initial notification within 4 hours of classification and no later than 24 hours from awareness; intermediate report within 72 hours of the initial notification; final report within one month of the latest intermediate report). The final-report wording was also read directly in an ESMA operational-instructions document (https://www.esma.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2026-09/DORA_Incident_reporting_-_Operational_instructions.pdf). The excerpt also mentions a noon-next-working-day relief for weekends and bank holidays whose exceptions were garbled; it is not modelled. Kavach computes only the 24-hour outer limit from first detection.

regimes.name: UK GDPR personal data breach
regimes.trigger: Breach likely to risk individuals' rights and freedoms
regimes.applies_to: UK controllers

stages.name: Report to ICO
stages.description: Within 72 hours of becoming aware; phased reporting allowed; explain any delay

regimes.regulator: Sectoral competent authorities (e.g. Ofcom, Ofgem, DWI, ICO for digital service providers)
regimes.name: NIS Regulations 2018 incident notification
regimes.trigger: Incident with significant impact on continuity of an essential service
regimes.applies_to: Operators of essential services and relevant digital service providers

stages.name: Notify competent authority
stages.description: Without undue delay and no later than 72 hours

regimes.notes: Confirmed 2026-11-16 from a search-result excerpt of regulation 11 (operator of essential services notifies its competent authority without undue delay and in any event no later than 72 hours after becoming aware). Direct fetch of legislation.gov.uk returned empty; the site shows differing versions of reg. 11 (the 2021 version also mentions digital service providers), so check the version in force. The government second post-implementation review asked whether 72 hours suffices; no change was found.

regimes.name: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident
regimes.trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
regimes.applies_to: SEC registrants (US-listed issuers)

stages.name: File Form 8-K Item 1.05
stages.description: Four business days after determining materiality; materiality must be determined without unreasonable delay; the US Attorney General may authorise delay for national security or public safety

regimes.notes: Kavach cannot know when materiality is determined, so no deadline is computed from findings (the clock starts at the determination, not detection).

regimes.name: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule
regimes.trigger: Discovery of a breach of unsecured protected health information
regimes.applies_to: HIPAA covered entities (business associates notify the covered entity)

stages.name: Notify individuals and HHS (500 or more)
stages.description: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery

stages.name: Annual HHS log (fewer than 500)
stages.description: Within 60 days after the end of the calendar year in which the breach was discovered

regimes.notes: Confirmed 2026-11-16: 45 CFR 164.404 read on eCFR (individuals: "without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 calendar days after discovery"). 164.408 read via the Cornell LII reproduction (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.408): 500 or more individuals, notify the Secretary at the same time as individuals; fewer than 500, within 60 days after the end of each calendar year. The media-notice rule (164.406) was not read.

regimes.name: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reporting
regimes.trigger: Covered entity reasonably believes a covered cyber incident occurred; or pays a ransom
regimes.applies_to: Critical infrastructure covered entities (proposed rule)

stages.name: Covered cyber incident report
stages.description: Proposed: within 72 hours of reasonable belief the incident occurred

stages.name: Ransom payment report
stages.description: Proposed: within 24 hours of making a ransom payment

regimes.notes: NOT YET IN EFFECT: the NPRM was published 2024-04-04 and the final rule has no stated effective date; reporting is not required until the final rule takes effect. Informational only until then.

regimes.name: Cybersecurity Act incident reporting
regimes.trigger: Prescribed cybersecurity incident affecting a CII or covered system
regimes.applies_to: CII owners (and entities covered by the 2025 amendments)

stages.name: Initial notification (verbal)
stages.description: Within 2 hours of becoming aware

stages.name: Supplementary details
stages.description: Written supplementary details within 72 hours after becoming aware (CSA forms page, section 3.3)

stages.name: Final report
stages.description: Within 30 days after submission of the supplementary details (CSA forms page, section 3.4)

regimes.notes: Corrected 2026-11-16: the CSA forms page (read directly, section 3.2-3.4) gives 2 hours from awareness (phone/text), supplementary details within 72 hours of becoming aware, and a final report within 30 days after submission of the supplementary details. The earlier 14-day figure does not appear there (a search excerpt indicates it belonged to the 2018 rules, amended from 31 Oct 2025). The final report is now measured from the supplementary submission, not from awareness. Applies to owners of provider-owned CII; other owner types (third-party-owned, systems of temporary concern) have separate regulations not checked.

regimes.name: PDPA data breach notification
regimes.trigger: Breach assessed to be notifiable (significant harm or 500 or more individuals)
regimes.applies_to: Organisations under the PDPA

stages.name: Notify PDPC
stages.description: Within 3 calendar days of assessing the breach as notifiable (measured here from first detection as a conservative proxy)

regimes.notes: Confirmed 2026-11-16: PDPC guide (read directly; dated 15 Mar 2021) shows assessment within 30 calendar days and notification to the PDPC within 3 calendar days after the assessment that the breach is notifiable. The statute text (PDPA s26D) was seen only via a search excerpt. Kavach measures the 3 days from first detection as a conservative outer bound. Check the PDPC site for guide revisions after 2021.

regimes.name: SOCI Act critical cyber security incident
regimes.trigger: Incident with significant impact on availability of a critical infrastructure asset
regimes.applies_to: Responsible entities of critical infrastructure assets

stages.name: Report to ASD
stages.description: Within 12 hours of becoming aware; written record within 84 hours if reported verbally

regimes.notes: Confirmed 2026-11-16 from a search-result excerpt of the ASD page: critical incident reported within 12 hours of becoming aware; if reported verbally, a written record within 84 hours. Direct fetch of the page timed out. A statutory cite (s30BC) comes from a Home Affairs exposure-draft explanatory statement, not read directly.

regimes.name: SOCI Act other cyber security incident
regimes.trigger: Incident with relevant impact on a critical infrastructure asset
regimes.applies_to: Responsible entities of critical infrastructure assets

stages.name: Report to ASD
stages.description: Within 72 hours of becoming aware; written record within 48 hours if reported verbally

regimes.notes: Confirmed 2026-11-16 from a search-result excerpt of the ASD page: other (relevant-impact) incident within 72 hours of becoming aware; written record within 48 hours if reported verbally. Direct fetch timed out. A submission recommending a single 72-hour window is a recommendation only.

regimes.regulator: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)
regimes.name: Notifiable Data Breaches scheme
regimes.trigger: Eligible data breach likely to result in serious harm
regimes.applies_to: Organisations covered by the Privacy Act 1988

stages.name: Complete assessment
stages.description: Reasonable steps to assess within 30 days of suspicion; notify OAIC and individuals as soon as practicable once an eligible breach is confirmed

regimes.notes: Confirmed 2026-11-16 from search-result excerpts of OAIC guidance: reasonable steps to complete the assessment within 30 days of suspicion (OAIC treats 30 days as a ceiling); notify OAIC and individuals as soon as practicable once an eligible breach is believed. Direct fetch of oaic.gov.au returned 403. Privacy Act amendments after 2024 were not checked.

regimes.name: APPI leakage report
regimes.trigger: Leak, loss or damage of personal data likely to harm individuals' rights (e.g. sensitive data, unauthorised access, 1,000+ people)
regimes.applies_to: Business operators handling personal information

stages.name: Preliminary report
stages.description: Promptly, commonly described as about 3 to 5 days

stages.name: Final report (wrongful-purpose cases)
stages.description: Within 60 days where wrongful acts are involved; otherwise 30 days

regimes.notes: Confirmed 2026-11-16: PPC page (read directly) gives a preliminary report within 3 to 5 days of discovery, a final report within 30 days, and 60 days where the incident may have been committed for an improper purpose. Whether any exemption from the preliminary report has since been adopted was not checked.

regimes.name: CERT-In Directions of 28 April 2022
regimes.trigger: Occurrence of a listed cyber security incident (Annexure I)
regimes.applies_to: Service providers, intermediaries, data centres, body corporates, government organisations

stages.name: Report to CERT-In
stages.description: Within 6 hours of noticing or being notified of the incident

regimes.notes: Confirmed 2026-11-16: the Directions PDF (read directly) requires listed cyber incidents (Annexure I) to be reported "within 6 hours of noticing such" an incident. Later amendments or FAQ changes were not checked. This is the clock Kavach already shows at /v1/compliance/cert-in-clock.

regimes.name: DPDP Rules 2025 personal data breach (Rule 7)
regimes.trigger: Personal data breach
regimes.applies_to: Data fiduciaries

stages.name: Detailed report to the Board
stages.description: Intimate the Board without delay; detailed report within 72 hours (Board may extend). Rule 7 applies from about 13 May 2027 (18 months after gazette publication)

regimes.notes: Corrected 2026-11-16: Rule 7(2) (read in the gazetted Rules, dated 13 Nov 2025) requires intimation to the Board without delay and detailed information within 72 hours of becoming aware (or longer if the Board allows on written request). Rule 1(4): rules 5 to 16 (including Rule 7) come into force eighteen months after gazette publication, so about 13 May 2027; the clock is not yet legally binding. Some PIB pages give 14 Nov as the notification date; the gazette itself is dated 13 Nov.

regimes.regulator: Autoridade Nacional de Protecao de Dados (ANPD)
regimes.name: LGPD security incident (Resolution CD/ANPD 15/2024)
regimes.trigger: Incident that may cause relevant risk or damage to data subjects
regimes.applies_to: Controllers under LGPD

stages.name: Notify ANPD and data subjects
stages.description: Within 3 business days of knowing the incident affected personal data; supplementary information within 20 business days; small agents get double time

regimes.notes: Confirmed 2026-11-16: Resolution CD/ANPD 15/2024 art. 6 (read on a Ministry of Justice digital-library copy): three business days, counted from the controller knowing the incident affected personal data; supplementary information within 20 business days of the communication. Specific legislation with its own deadline prevails. The official Diario Oficial copy was not read.

regimes.name: NCA Essential Cybersecurity Controls incident reporting
regimes.trigger: Cybersecurity incident at an entity subject to NCA controls
regimes.applies_to: Government and critical national infrastructure entities

stages.name: Notify NCA
stages.description: Timeline not found

regimes.notes: Confirmed 2026-11-16: ECC-1:2018 (PDF text read directly) lists control 2-13-3-3 "Cybersecurity incidents reporting to NCA" and no numeric time limit anywhere in the document. NCA may set timelines in other instruments, which were not checked.

regimes.name: PDPL breach notification
regimes.trigger: Breach likely to harm data subjects or conflict with their rights (draft amendments would remove the harm test)
regimes.applies_to: Controllers under the PDPL

stages.name: Notify SDAIA
stages.description: Within 72 hours of awareness; written justification if later

regimes.notes: Confirmed 2026-11-16 from search-result excerpts of the SDAIA Implementing Regulation (Art. 24: notify the competent authority within 72 hours of becoming aware; missing details later with justification) and SDAIA breach guide. Direct fetch of sdaia.gov.sa was rejected. Amendments after the excerpted versions were not checked.

regimes.name: Federal PDPL breach notification
regimes.trigger: Breach affecting data subjects' privacy, confidentiality or security
regimes.applies_to: Controllers under Federal Decree-Law 45 of 2021 (DIFC and ADGM have separate regimes)

stages.name: Notify Data Office
stages.description: Immediate notification expected; no fixed time limit published

regimes.notes: UNVERIFIED. 2026-11-16: a search excerpt of the UAE Legislation portal text of Decree-Law 45/2021 Art. 9 says the controller notifies the regulator when it becomes aware of a breach, "in accordance with the period and measures" set by the Executive Regulations. Whether Executive Regulations fixing a deadline are in force could not be confirmed (portal fetch returned HTTP 403), so the "no fixed time limit" claim stays unverified.

regimes.name: POPIA section 22 security compromise
regimes.trigger: Reasonable grounds to believe personal information was accessed or acquired by an unauthorised person
regimes.applies_to: Responsible parties under POPIA

stages.name: Notify Regulator and data subjects
stages.description: As soon as reasonably possible after discovery; no fixed hour limit

regimes.notes: Confirmed 2026-11-16: POPIA s22(2) (read in the Regulator-hosted Act) requires notification "as soon as reasonably possible after the discovery of the compromise", allowing for law enforcement needs and scoping. No fixed hour limit. The Regulator says reporting is through its eServices portal from 1 April 2025 (search excerpt).

regimes.regulator: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada (OPC)
regimes.name: PIPEDA breach of security safeguards
regimes.trigger: Breach creating a real risk of significant harm
regimes.applies_to: Private-sector organisations under PIPEDA

stages.name: Report to OPC and notify individuals
stages.description: As soon as feasible after determining the breach meets the threshold; keep records for 24 months

regimes.notes: Confirmed 2026-11-16: PIPEDA s10.1 (read on Justice Laws) requires reporting to the Commissioner "as soon as feasible after the organization determines that the breach has occurred" when there is a real risk of significant harm; s10.3 requires records of every breach. The OPC page https://www.priv.gc.ca/en/privacy-topics/business-privacy/breaches-and-safeguards/privacy-breaches-at-your-business/gd_pb_201810/ (read) states two years (24 months) retention.

regimes.name: PIPA breach notification (Art. 34)
regimes.trigger: Leak of personal information (thresholds apply for regulator reporting, e.g. 1,000+ data subjects)
regimes.applies_to: Personal information controllers

stages.name: Notify data subjects; report to PIPC/KISA in listed cases
stages.description: Within 72 hours of becoming aware (Decree Art. 39 for individuals; Art. 40 for the report, only for 1,000+ data subjects, sensitive or unique identifiers, or illegal external access)

regimes.notes: Corrected 2026-11-16: the 72-hour limits are in the Enforcement Decree, not the Act (KLRI English translation, text amended through Presidential Decree 35343 of 25 Feb 2025; read directly). Art. 39: notify data subjects within 72 hours (later once the cause ceases in listed cases). Art. 40: report to the PIPC or KISA within 72 hours only where 1,000 or more data subjects are affected, sensitive or unique identifiers are involved, or illegal external access occurred. KLRI is a government translation, not the Korean original; a 2026 amendment was not checked (a search excerpt showed a consolidated text effective 2026-09-11).

regimes.regulator: Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data (PCPD)
regimes.name: PDPO data breach notification
regimes.trigger: Data breach with real risk of harm (notification currently guidance, not mandatory; reform proposed)
regimes.applies_to: Data users under the PDPO

stages.name: Notify PCPD (guidance)
stages.description: As soon as practicable; no statutory hour limit

regimes.notes: UNVERIFIED. 2026-11-16: search excerpts of the PCPD June 2023 guidance say notify "as soon as practicable" and an August 2024 PCPD presentation lists notification as not a statutory requirement. The PCPD PDF fetch returned empty and nothing from 2025-2026 was found, so a later statutory change cannot be ruled out.
